about: R27 review ledger (D110). One entry per safety-class Spanish string: the exact English, the exact Spanish, sha = sha256(en + U+0000 + es), and how far its review has got — draft (written), reviewed (blind second pass agreed AND back-translated to English without the original), person (a Spanish-reading crew member read it on a phone, R27 #5 / R29 #3). Safety-class Spanish is served only at reviewed or person. Editing either side without re-reviewing fails the build (src/i18n/ledger.ts ledgerProblems).

entries.note: Recorded 2026-10-22 (D112). Back: same meaning, the hedge kept (probably, not certainly). Second: "PERMISO PROBABLEMENTE REQUERIDO" — same meaning. Flagged and accepted: "permiso" also means permission — it is the Spanish word for permit (the blind second pass chose it too), and either reading stops to ask.

entries.backTranslation: VERIFY WITH THE CITY — THE MAP DID NOT SHOW A PROTECTED ZONE
entries.note: Recorded 2026-10-22 (D112). Back: same meaning, the order first. Second: "VERIFIQUE CON LA CIUDAD — EL MAPA NO MUESTRA ZONA PROTEGIDA" — same meaning, same order. Flagged and accepted: "no mostró" can also read "failed to show" — the more cautious reading; the second clause can read as reassurance — VERIFY leads, unconditionally (the English leads with NO OVERLAY, so the Spanish is the stronger order); "verifique" speaks to the reader as VERIFY does.

entries.es: NO SE MANEJA — FRENOS/DIRECCIÓN
entries.translatedBy: Claude — docs/R27_SPANISH_PLAN.md table (2026-10-20), after the plan’s two adversarial critiques
entries.note: Not recorded (D112) — drift. Blind back: "no se maneja" is impersonal and reads as a description too ("it does not get driven"), not an order; in Spain "manejar" is handle ("we do not handle brakes/steering" — no order at all); "dirección" also reads as address. Blind second (from the English): "NO CONDUZCA — FUERA DE SERVICIO" — a direct order and the whole unit out of service, where this says only "not driven" — a meaning difference: HELD keeps the unit off the schedule until Mike signs it back on (src/fleet/breakdown.ts). Proposed, not applied (it needs a fresh blind pass): "NO LO MANEJE NI LO USE — FUERA DE SERVICIO (FRENOS O DIRECCIÓN)".

For the read-through: the second pass’s "ni trepar ni canasta" spells the scope out.

entries.backTranslation: POWER LINES — it is mandatory to coordinate with the electric company before working near the wires

Flagged and accepted: it names no one to coordinate — the English names no one; "cables" is wider than power conductors — wider is more caution, under LÍNEAS ELÉCTRICAS.

entries.en: PERMIT LIKELY — do not start protected work until the permit is confirmed.
entries.es: PROBABLEMENTE SE NECESITA PERMISO — no empiece el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work) hasta que se confirme el permiso.
entries.translatedBy: Claude — R27 Phase A unit 1, first translation pass (D111)
entries.backTranslation: A PERMIT IS PROBABLY NEEDED — do not start the work that requires a permit (protected work) until the permit is confirmed.
entries.note: Not recorded (D112). The blind back-translation (2026-10-22) found no drift, and "el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work)" came back as "the work that requires a permit (protected work)" without the English. Held because no blind second translation has agreed with these words: the only one (D111’s review round) wrote "el trabajo en zona protegida (protected work)" — work in a protected zone, a different meaning (src/permitting/permitRecord.ts requiresClearance also counts a permit flag outside any zone) — and D111 chose these words after it. Owed: a blind second translation of L12, L14, L15 and L16 from the English alone, with the glossary (TRADE_TERMS: protected work → "el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work)"); then this entry can be recorded as is — its back-translation stands while the Spanish is unchanged.

entries.backTranslation: PERMIT: IT HAS TO BE REVIEWED — consult with the office before cutting.

entries.en: NO OVERLAY — VERIFY W/ CITY before protected work.
entries.es: VERIFIQUE CON LA CIUDAD — EL MAPA NO MOSTRÓ ZONA PROTEGIDA. Hágalo antes de empezar el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work).
entries.translatedBy: Claude — R27 Phase A unit 1, first translation pass (D111)
entries.backTranslation: VERIFY WITH THE CITY — THE MAP DID NOT SHOW A PROTECTED ZONE. Do it before starting the work that requires a permit (protected work).
entries.note: Not recorded (D112). The blind back-translation (2026-10-22) found no drift, and "el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work)" came back as "the work that requires a permit (protected work)" without the English. Held because no blind second translation has agreed with these words: the only one (D111’s review round) wrote "el trabajo en zona protegida (protected work)" — work in a protected zone, a different meaning (src/permitting/permitRecord.ts requiresClearance also counts a permit flag outside any zone) — and D111 chose these words after it. Also for that pass (the back-translator’s flags; the English has the same shape): "Hágalo" tells the reader to verify with the city himself, as VERIFY does; the second clause can read as reassurance; "if there is no protected zone, which work needs a permit?" — the English "NO OVERLAY … before protected work" asks the same. Owed: a blind second translation of L12, L14, L15 and L16 from the English alone, with the glossary (TRADE_TERMS: protected work → "el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work)"); then this entry can be recorded as is — its back-translation stands while the Spanish is unchanged.
